resources.title: What to look for in a pharmaceutical manufacturing partner
resources.summary: A practical starting point for discussing quality systems, manufacturing scope, and supporting documentation.
body: Start with the scope: dosage form, manufacturing site, proposed market, and the activities covered by the relevant authorization. A general statement about quality is not a substitute for current, site-specific documentation.

A useful quality discussion covers trained personnel, documented processes, material controls, validation, testing, and the handling of deviations and complaints. These are connected parts of a pharmaceutical quality system.
Before making a sourcing decision, request the applicable licenses and certificates, establish the quality agreement, and arrange technical or quality due diligence appropriate to the project.

resources.title: Product documentation starts with the destination market
resources.summary: Why product, site, and market details belong at the beginning of every export conversation.
body: The same formulation can have different registration requirements in different countries. Begin a discussion with the product name, dosage form, strength, proposed manufacturer, and destination market.

Under the WHO certification scheme, a Certificate of a Pharmaceutical Product (CPP) communicates the status of a product and applicant in the exporting country. It should not be treated as a blanket approval for every product or market.
Ask which documents apply to your project, who issues them, and whether they are current. The importing country’s authority determines the requirements for local authorization.
resources.sourceTitle: WHO — Certification scheme for pharmaceutical products

resources.title: Quality belongs throughout the manufacturing process
resources.summary: Understanding why finished-product testing is one part of a much wider control system.
body: Good manufacturing practice is designed to reduce risks that cannot be addressed by testing the finished product alone. Consistent processes and documented controls matter from incoming materials through production.

During a technical discussion, ask how the proposed product will be manufactured, packaged, tested, and released. Clear responsibilities and documented procedures make the conversation more useful than broad promises of perfection.
This overview is business information. Product-specific specifications, validation requirements, and quality arrangements should be established with the responsible technical and regulatory teams.
